title: provision: singleton mailbox set, no user_id
description:
## Why
provision_user_mailboxes is called per JMAP request and takes a user_id. With the shared-mailbox schema, there is one set of six special folders for the whole server, provisioned once at startup.

## What

### provision.rs rewrites
- Remove user_id parameter from mailbox_id_for_user (or replace with a server-constant).
  Decision needed: mailbox IDs can remain SHA-256 derived but seeded from role alone (not user_id), since there is only one user context. Simpler: use hardcoded stable IDs generated once and stored in the new mailboxes table.
- Rename provision_user_mailboxes to provision_mailboxes(); no user_id argument.
  INSERT OR IGNORE INTO mailboxes (mailbox_id, role, name, sort_order) VALUES (...) — same 6 rows, no user_id.
- Remove resolve_user_id entirely (no longer needed).
- Remove list_user_mailboxes user_id param; query becomes SELECT ... FROM mailboxes ORDER BY sort_order.
- Call provision_mailboxes() once at JmapStores::new() or server startup, not per request.

### mail/src/server.rs
- Remove the resolve_user_id + provision_user_mailboxes block from route_method.
- Remove user_id local variable from route_method entirely.
- Update Mailbox/get, Email/query, Email/get arms to not pass user_id.

## Acceptance criteria
- provision_mailboxes() creates 6 rows in mailboxes on first run, is idempotent on subsequent runs.
- route_method has no user_id variable and no resolve_user_id call.
- All tests pass.
